result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A has the stronger campaign: it builds on a specific reason people buy gifts (they're bought in a panic but should look thoughtful) and uses made-to-order as an honest reason to order now. Its copy also uses clear placeholders throughout. A's weakness is that it never says outright that it is dropping the 200-box claim, the Friday sell-out or the restarting timer. It only hints at this with 'same time for every visitor' and 'publish only a number you'd actually stop at.' B has the stronger concept (gifts bought in a last-minute panic but meant to look thoughtful) and cleaner placeholders, but it never says it dropped the user's requests, so the user may not notice the change. A's example countdown value (56 days) is invented and not marked as a placeholder, and its idea is thinner than B's.
